label: Mathematical and ecclesiastical Latin as a design strategy
statement: The lexical overlap between mathematical Latin and ecclesiastical Latin was used as a deliberate design strategy.
scope: Interpretive layer. Every translation used as evidence is itself an interpretation and must show the word by word correspondence.
falsified_if: Proposed by Claude, for the researcher to accept or replace: the terms claimed to bridge the two registers are not attested in both registers in texts available in Milan around 1495.
Proposed by Claude: the overlap in the chosen vocabulary is no higher than in a baseline sample of terms drawn at random from the same mathematical and liturgical texts.
Proposed by Claude: no channel is documented by which the designer could have used the overlap (no relevant text in Leonardo's library lists or notebooks, no link through Pacioli).
open_questions: Fix the corpus: which mathematical texts (e.g. Pacioli's Summa, De divina proportione) and which liturgical texts are admitted as the two registers?
